note: 'Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a serpent' (Exod 7:10). **Whose rod it is shifts between the two of them**, and the book uses both names for it.

'they asked Ezra the scribe to bring out the Book of the Law of Moses' (Neh 8:1), and he read it 'from the morning until midday' (8:3). **A book written in Moab, read aloud in Jerusalem a thousand years later.**

'just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites. He built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses' (Josh 8:31), and the charge to keep it at 23:6. **Joshua cites the book by name** -- one of the earliest places the corpus quotes a written source it can point at.
'And he took the staff of God in his hand.' (Exod 4:20), and it is in his hand again before Pharaoh and over the sea.
'the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands' (Exod 32:15) coming down the first time, and again at 34:29 with his face shining.
'Chisel out two stone tablets like the originals' (Exod 34:1), and he does at 34:4. **The second set is his work and the first was not.**
'When Moses had finished writing in a book the words of this law' (Deut 31:24).

'He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant-the Ten Commandments.' (Exod 34:28). The graph already held God speaking them at Exod 20:1; **this is the other half, and Moses had no edge to them at all.**
'Then Moses went up to God' (Exod 19:3), and up again with the second tables at 34:4.
